name: Lady of the Lake

attributes.attribute: gave the sword Excalibur to Arthur
protected Arthur for his whole life

sources: Evans-Wentz, W. Y. The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries. Gerrards Cross: Colin Smythe Humanities Press, 1911, 327.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Lady of the Lake was an Arthurian heroine. Some tales call her Nimue or Morgause, though she is set apart from those figures. She gave the sword Excalibur to the king-to-be Arthur. In early texts she was a fairy, a semidivine being in the Celtic Otherworld, which in her case was the Land of Women. She lived on a magical lake with her maiden servants. She captured Lancelot and raised him to be her protector, which gave him the name Lancelot of the Lake. Some sources say Lancelot was her lover and father of the pure knight Galahad. Later writers lowered her to a sorceress who made an illusory lake. Still, her power lasted, for she guarded Arthur through his life, and he returned to her at the end.

okr.objective: Present the Lady of the Lake as the fairy who gave Arthur the sword Excalibur.
key_results: Note the alternate names Nimue and Morgause.
